title: Republic Book IX: why the tyrannical soul is wretched and the just man is happiest
summary: Socrates traces how an unruled soul becomes tyrannical and argues that the tyrant, though seemingly powerful, is the most miserable and unfree of men. He gives three proofs that the just, reason-ruled man lives most happily: only wisdom delivers true pleasure, and injustice ruins the soul even when it goes undetected.

principles.text: The tyrant, for all his power, is a slave: he is ruled by his worst desires and cannot do what he wants.
principles.quote: He who is the real tyrant, whatever men may think, is the real slave, and is obliged to practise the greatest adulation and servility, and to be the flatterer of the vilest of mankind.

principles.text: The best and justest man is also the happiest; the worst and most unjust is the most miserable, seen or unseen by gods and men.
principles.quote: the best and justest is also the happiest, and that this is he who is the most royal man and king over himself

principles.text: Tyrants never have true friends or freedom; they are only ever masters or servants.
principles.quote: They are always either the masters or servants and never the friends of anybody; the tyrant never tastes of true freedom or friendship.

principles.text: Judge life by experience, wisdom and reason: the philosopher has tasted all pleasures and alone knows the pleasure of truth.
principles.quote: Well, but what ought to be the criterion? Is any better than experience and wisdom and reason?

principles.text: Injustice gains nothing even if undetected; punishment frees the gentler part of the soul and perfects it.
principles.quote: He who is undetected only gets worse, whereas he who is detected and punished has the brutal part of his nature silenced and humanized

principles.text: Let the man within rule the whole person, tending the gentle qualities and allying with the lion-heart, not feeding the many-headed beast.
principles.quote: he should ever so speak and act as to give the man within him in some way or other the most complete mastery over the entire human creature.
